reports.note: Actual Game.tick, normal bullets/HP/AI/offered upgrades, explicit dense spawn isolation. Legacy bullet baseline is used only when legacyBulletComparison=true; otherwise both passes retain default bullet rules and onPass controls the renderer experiment. One fixed1/60 tick per render; raf mode waits before every render, batch8 keeps historical eight-render yields. This is a paced fixed-workload comparison: no product-loop catch-up, interpolation, HUD, audio or persistence. Render time is game.time for deterministic camera/shake. Call wall times include instrumentation; combined includes event draining and render. rAF callback intervals include browser scheduling and are not presented FPS or actual GPU execution. QA data stays in memory.

note: QA-only fresh-owned CPU alpha / exact GPU min12 / CPU alpha A/B/A, each combat arm shares bounded original-model texture union upload and original-material shader API preparation before drawing. Only B additionally prepares the two alpha shaders with a15s idle lease; verify=false in combat. gpuStats.frames and gpuUsedCells count cells, not presented frames; min12 makes each successful alpha read48 bytes. Startup, first frame, all110 callbacks and100 steady callbacks are reported separately, including startup totals. Original7-type×8-pose correctness is a separate fresh fixture whose helper individually loads types after initial walker preparation; it retains verify=true/min1 original RGBA, geometry, animation and private-image checks. All combat uses original Game seed774, fixed1/60 ticks, normal offered upgrades,110 renders and existing state/RNG/event/pixel comparisons. Native12/256 and boss512 remain unchanged; pose bounds, crop, direct readback and batch ink stay OFF. Instrumented fixed-workload call wall times and shader API readiness are not GPU completion, presented FPS, total heap or actual app-loop performance. A genuine memory-store brand gates execution only: no storage API is called and actual app persistence is not tested. The original renderer rig is never disposed; all experimental rigs are retired and original owner descriptors restored unless externally replaced.
